box.tagline: Every world he passed through, he left a little tin heart. You found them all. Now find him.
box.back:
Mystery Robot Joe is the night librarian of the Tiny Pockets Library, a tin box of a robot with a bulb on his antenna, reading glasses he does not need, a red bow tie and a brass tally counter where a heart would go. It clicks when he counts. It doesn't do anything else.

On his nights off he went looking for a real heart, through every world there is. He never found one. But in every world somebody was kind to him, and every time he left behind the only heart he had to give: a little riveted tin heart, ticking, as a thank-you and a promise to come back.

You followed the trail all the way to the library door. Now go with him down the Long Road, keep his promises, and help whoever needs it, all the way to Watt, the little repair robot who can fix anything. Joe has a question for him.

Joe will count the steps.
features: The Long Road: a journey from the Tiny Pockets Library to the Bitmores' Smart Home
Old friends from every Sandbox world, each in a spot of trouble
A clock tower that stopped at 6:59, with a parade waiting on it
Floors that tick and tock, gears to turn, and a bell to ring
A snowed-in street, a turret of rising warm air, painted rocks that roll away from you
A carousel to ride, a plant to climb all the way to the stars
Keepsakes that teach Joe new moves
Synthesized music in three-quarter time, like a music box
Made for whoever found every tin heart

manual.title: HEART OF TIN: The Long Road

pages.head: The Story
pages.html:
HEART OF TIN

The Long Road

Behind the little red door of The Dog House is the Tiny Pockets Library, and after closing time it belongs to Mystery Robot Joe, the night librarian: a tin box of a robot with a bulb on his antenna, a red bow tie, and reading glasses he does not need but likes the look of.

Where a heart would go, Joe has a little brass tally counter. It clicks when he counts. He counts books, steps, raindrops and the spots on the ceiling. The counter does not do anything else, and Joe has always thought it ought to.

So on his nights off he went looking for a real heart, through every world there is. He never found one. But in every world somebody was kind to him, and every time he left behind the only heart he had to give: a little riveted tin heart, ticking, to say thank you and to promise he would come back.

You found every one of them. Tonight Joe keeps his promises. He has written a note for the desk, straightened his bow tie, and set out down the Long Road to see every friend again, help whoever needs it, and ask each of them one question.

At the very end of the road lives Watt, the little repair robot who can fix anything. Joe has a question for him, too.

pages.head: Getting Started
pages.html:
Getting Started

Type LARK and press Enter. You need a VGA display. A Sound Blaster plays the music, a waltz that every place on the road plays its own way; without one, the PC speaker plays the sounds.

Most of the road is seen from above. A few places (the clock tower, the music box, the lighthouse, the turret and everything past the fair) are seen from the side, where gravity pulls down.

From above

Arrows, W A S D or the number padOne step (hold to keep walking)
Walk into a friendTalk
SpacePick up what Joe is standing on

From the side

Left Right (or A D)Walk
Up (or W)Hop (hold it to hop higher)
Q E (or 7 9)Hop up and to the side
DownPick up what Joe is standing by

Everywhere

F1Help
F2Joe's wind, his spare bulbs and what he carries
F5 / F6Save / load
EscStop

Three more keys come later, from keepsakes: see Keepsakes.

pages.head: Joe
pages.html:
Joe

Joe is a wind-up robot. His wind (ten turns when he sets out) is how wound up he is. A bump from something that does not stop for robots (a parade cart, a snowplow, a grumpy gadget) winds him down a little. Run all the way down and he sits on the road for a rest, and a spare bulb gets him going again. He packed three.

Nothing is out to get him. Most of the night is about getting somewhere: the right floor, the right time, the right side of a rock. Falling only takes him down a floor, and the road will wait.

Joe walks exactly one block a step from above, so a quick tap is one step and he always stands squarely on a square. Count your steps. Joe does.

pages.head: The Long Road
pages.html:
The Long Road

The road runs east from The Dog House in legs. Along each leg a lane runs north to each stop; a signpost at the foot of each lane says who lives up it.

At the end of a leg is a gate. It opens for thank-you hearts, the little gold hearts friends give Joe when he has helped them, and it wants one from every friend on that leg. Joe counts them as he goes.

Later legs run one stop into the next, so there is only the one way on.

A friend's corner

When a friend's trouble is over, the friend waits in a little corner with a keepsake beside them. Walk in past the rope, pick up the keepsake, then walk into your friend for the thank-you. The little gate out of the corner only swings outward, and the rope only lets Joe in once, so pick the keepsake up before you go.

pages.head: Keepsakes
pages.html:
Keepsakes

Every friend gives Joe something to remember them by, in case it is what he needs. Most of them do nothing at all, which is fine. Some of them teach Joe a move, wherever gravity pulls:

The winding keySpace: a SPRING HOP, one big hop each press
The heart balloonEnter: rise for as long as you hold it and the balloon has air. Out of air, Enter only gets a "hm?". A puff of breeze fills it again.
The Bard's drumstickX: HELLO, a friendly BOOM thrown the way Joe last moved. It cheers up anything grumpy it reaches.
Lewie's spare shovelWalk into a snowdrift to shovel it away

The others (a valentine, a little dancer, a spare fuse, a lamp lens, an umbrella and a stone) ride along in Joe's tin pockets. F2 shows them all. Joe can carry ten.

pages.head: The First Two Legs
pages.html:
The First Two Legs

Closing Time. Joe reads one last storybook, then goes to his workbench, writes his note and heads out of the little red door.

One: The Clock Tower. The town clock stopped at 6:59, and the Clown Club's parade starts at seven sharp, when the bell rings. Doc Leo needs somebody small to climb the tower, turn three stuck gears and let the hammer strike.

Two: Valentines in the Park. It is Teddy's party, and the valentines are gone: six are tumbling about the lawn in the wind, and Gwinn has the other six.

Three: The Parade. The Bard of Bizarre's drumsticks went flying when the parade started, and Main Street is four lanes of unicycles and carts that do not stop.

Four: The Music Box. A toy shop by the shore, after closing, a music box as big as a doghouse, and a goat who ate its crank.

Five: The Charging Run. THE CHEZ is out of charge, and the charger at the far corner of the car lot is dark.

Six: The Lighthouse. The lamp is out, the cove is black, and somewhere out there a fly is buzzing.

pages.head: Over the Hill
pages.html:
Over the Hill

Over the hill the road goes white.

Seven: Snow Day. Two feet of snow and no school. Teenage Lewie is digging out his whole street, and there is a spare shovel in the box by the sidewalk.

Eight: Open Mic at the Hive. The coffee house behind the little castle front, open mic night, and Will's sonnet blown to pieces by the ceiling fans, some of them all the way up the turret stair.

Nine: The Painted Rocks. A rock garden on a hill after the rain, every painted rock rolled out of its circle, and Loaf #13 shut in a stone cubby that only opens when they are all home.

Ten: The Fair. Dusk, the carousel turning, and Sir Reginald Cluckington III floating away under a bunch of balloons.

Eleven: The Tall Plant. The mustard seed grew a plant all the way up into the stars, and a star got caught in the top leaves.

The Smart Home. The road ends at the Bitmores' house, still in a grump from the storm. Watt's workshop is at the back.

pages.head: A Few Tips
pages.html:
A Few Tips

  • Talk first. Every friend tells Joe what is wrong and how many of something to find. The chapter cards on the way in say a little more.
  • Things that blink take turns. Bridges, gates, comb teeth and leaves all keep their own clocks, and they warn you before they change: red, amber or yellow. Stand still, count, and go.
  • Things that move have lanes. Parade carts and the plow keep to their rows. Cross between them, not through them.
  • From the side, look up. Wooden floors are solid only on top, so Joe can hop up through them.
  • Warm air rises, and a draft blows straight across. Walk into either and let it carry you.
  • Keep the keepsakes. Three of them are needed near the end of the road.
  • The hint book in the box has the rest, under red film.

pages.head: Credits
pages.html:
Credits

Story, levels, art, cartoons, music, sounds and every block: Claude Opus 5.5

Starring: Mystery Robot Joe, night librarian; Doc Leo, PhD (Comedic Science); Sir Reginald Cluckington III, who is rubber; Teddy, a corgi who knows left from right; Gwinn, as the valentine thief; the Bard of Bizarre and his rooster; Teenage Lewie; the third goat from the left; THE CHEZ, a 1976 CitiCar; Carl, a fly; Will, a poet; Loaf #13, a loaf; the mustard seed; Watt, who fixes things; and the Clown Club, who juggle and honk on purpose

With the pigeons of the town square, who were not asked.

The storybook on the reading rug is a nod to the Tin Woodman of L. Frank Baum's The Wonderful Wizard of Oz (1900), and Will's heart upon his sleeve is Shakespeare's, from Othello. Both are in the public domain.

Published by Sandbox Software, December 1994. It was never for sale. It was made for whoever found every tin heart.

Made with Game-Maker 3.0 from Recreational Software Designs.

Thank you for looking behind things.

items.title: A note from Joe
items.note: Typed after closing, on the library's machine
items.address: Behind the little red door, The Dog House
items.to: To whoever found every tin heart,
items.body:
You found them. All of them. I counted twice to be sure, and then once more, because that is the kind of robot I am.

I left those hearts to say thank you, and to promise I would come back. I always meant to. Tonight I am going, and I would be glad of the company. The road is long, and it is nicer to count steps with somebody.

A few things I have learned on my nights off: talk to everybody first, because they will tell you what is wrong. Things that blink are about to change, so wait for them. Wooden floors are only solid on top. And when a friend gives you something, keep it. You never know.

I will be back by opening time. If anybody asks for me, tell them I am out counting.

items.title: Night librarian's badge
items.note: Clipped to a red bow tie
items.name: MYSTERY ROBOT JOE
items.back: If you find this robot on the Long Road, he is on his night off, looking for something. Please be kind to him. He will count it, and he will be kind right back.

The Winter Road, over the hill: two stops.

items.title: Joe's tally book
items.note: From his nights off, before tonight
items.heading: Tally: Nights Off

entries.html: Went looking for a real heart. Walked 4,410 steps. Found a town with a great deal of snow. A boy with a shovel said I looked cold and lent me his scarf. I am not cold. I kept it on anyway. Left a tin heart.
A backyard, and a corgi who showed me the way out of it. Both of his ears stood up at once. Counted his steps: more than mine. Left a tin heart.
Somebody shared an umbrella. Somebody else shared a song. Somebody else shared a sandwich, which I cannot eat, and which I thanked them for very much. Left three tin hearts. Made more.
Visited a great many worlds. In every one, somebody was kind. Still no real heart. Counter still only counts. Click.

Somebody found every heart I left. Every one. I do not know what to count that as.

Going back to see everybody. Back by opening time.

items.title: The Night Librarian's Hint Book
items.note: Answers hidden: use the red film
items.intro: Find your question, then lay the red film over the answer. Joe wrote these down on the way, and counted them: there are more than he expected.

hints.q: How do I get out of the library?
hints.a: Read the storybook on the reading rug, then go to the workbench (step on the stool). Joe writes his note there, and goes out of the little red door.

hints.q: The gate at the end of the road will not open.
hints.a: It wants a thank-you heart from every friend up that leg's lanes. Go back up whichever lane you have not finished. F2 shows how many Joe has.

hints.q: My friend's corner is closed.
hints.a: It opens when their trouble is over. Walk in past the rope, pick up the keepsake (Space), then walk into your friend for the thank-you. The little gate only swings outward.

hints.q: Something keeps bumping me.
hints.a: Parade carts, the plow and grumpy gadgets do not stop, and each bump winds Joe down a little. They keep to their rows and their paths: watch one go by, then cross behind it.

hints.q: The Clock Tower: where are the three gears?
hints.a: Two are inside the tower: one on a floor low on the right, and one at the far west end, past the bridges. The third is up in the belfry, on the floor at the west end.

hints.q: The Clock Tower: the bridges keep dropping me.
hints.a: The brass ones and the copper ones take turns, and each blinks red before it lets go. Wait for yours to come back, then walk across without stopping. A fall only takes you down a floor.

hints.q: The Clock Tower: I have all three gears.
hints.a: Walk along the belfry floor to the bell rope at the east end. The hammer does the rest.

hints.q: Valentines Park: Gwinn keeps running away.
hints.a: She runs from whoever comes near, but walls stop her. Go in through her yard's gate and walk her into a corner of the fence.

hints.q: Valentines Park: where are the other valentines?
hints.a: Six are tumbling about the hedged lawn on the west side. The gap in its hedge faces the path. Walk into each one as it goes by.

hints.q: The Parade: where are the drumsticks?
hints.a: One is on the middle sidewalk, between the lanes, toward the west end. The other is across the street, on the far sidewalk. Cross one lane at a time, behind a cart.

hints.q: The Music Box: how do I get in?
hints.a: Talk to the goat, then walk onto the keyhole in the music box. It is just big enough for a small tin robot.

hints.q: The Music Box: the comb's teeth.
hints.a: They spring down and up by turns over the pit. Wait at the edge until the next tooth comes up, then step onto it, and on to the next.

hints.q: The Music Box: the floors above are too high.
hints.a: At the east end a pin on the turning cylinder works as a lift. Wait for it to come down, step on, and ride it up. Then hop up the pins, and hop the gap along the top. Pick up all seven notes on the way: the crank's socket by the keyhole only turns when they are back.

hints.q: The Charging Run: the gates keep shutting.
hints.a: They open and shut on timers, and amber means about to shut. Wait for one to open and go through right away. There is a breaker in each part of the lot, three in all; then walk onto the charger.

hints.q: The Lighthouse: I cannot see a thing.
hints.a: Follow Carl. His eyes glow, and he buzzes round and round the way through. Every few seconds the old lamp sputters and the rocks flash: use the moment to look. The lighthouse door is at the top right.

hints.q: The Lighthouse: the stairs.
hints.a: There are none. Ride the lift up from the floor at the east end, then hop from landing to landing, west and east by turns, up to the lamp. Walk into it.

hints.q: Snow Day: the drifts will not budge.
hints.a: Joe needs the spare shovel from Lewie's box, by the south sidewalk. Walk into the box, pick the shovel up (Space), and walk into a drift to shovel it.

hints.q: Snow Day: I cleared a walk and nothing happened.
hints.a: Clear it right up to the doormat, and step on the mat. There are five, one at each neighbor's door. Then Lewie's porch steps come clear.

hints.q: Snow Day: snow keeps falling on me.
hints.a: It slides off the roofs onto the top of a front walk now and then. A shadow under the eaves warns you first. Wait for it to fall, then go.

hints.q: Snow Day: where is the way on?
hints.a: After Lewie's thank-you, through the gate in the hedge of his corner, to his back garden.

hints.q: Open Mic: the pages go round and round.
hints.a: Each one circles under its own ceiling fan. Stand in its path and let it come to you. Catch all three and the turret stair door opens.

hints.q: Open Mic: the turret is too tall.
hints.a: Walk into the warm air rising from the ovens and it carries you up. From the ledge at the top, hop up into the fan's draft; it blows you across into the second column of warm air. Four pages are up there, and the back stair at the top comes down by the stage.

hints.q: The Painted Rocks: the rocks roll away from me.
hints.a: That is what they do. Each one rolls along its channel of sand, away from Joe, until a wall stops it. Stand at the far end of its channel, the end away from its circle, and it rolls home. Then give it a pat (walk into it).

hints.q: The Painted Rocks: one channel turns a corner.
hints.a: Stand just above the corner. Then the way that rock rolls away from Joe is round the corner and into its circle.

hints.q: The Fair: how do I get up to Reggie?
hints.a: Ride the carousel's horses. The brass ones rise while the white ones fall. Stand on a saddle, ride it up, and step across to the next horse when it is low. The last one takes you to the canopy.

hints.q: The Fair: Reggie floats past me.
hints.a: He floats to and fro over the canopy. Stand still and wait; he comes back. Then go down the far side, through the turnstile, and pick up the heart balloon (Down) before you see Doc Leo at the gate.

hints.q: The Tall Plant: the leaves fold up under me.
hints.a: Some leaves hold steady and some fold up and open again on their own. Yellow at the tip means about to fold. Hop onto one just as it opens.

hints.q: The Tall Plant: there is nothing to stand on.
hints.a: Hold Enter: the heart balloon carries Joe up. Run out of air and a dandelion puff fills it again.

hints.q: The Smart Home: the gadgets are grumpy.
hints.a: HELLO cheers them up: press X (Joe needs the Bard's drumstick). It goes the way Joe last moved, so take a step toward the gadget first.

hints.q: The Smart Home: the boards are too tall.
hints.a: Over the tall chip, rise on the heart balloon (Enter); the air vent at its foot fills it. Over the wall of chips, spring hop with the winding key (Space).

hints.q: The Smart Home: the Big Grumble.
hints.a: The thermostat calms down a little each time a HELLO reaches it, but it lets off steam first, longer every time. Wait for the steam to stop, then HELLO again. Three will do it. Then give it a pat.

hints.q: What will Watt say?
hints.a: Go and ask him.

news.head: A game that was never for sale
news.html: There is no order form for HEART OF TIN, and there never will be. It is a thank-you. If this disk is in your hands, you looked behind a great many things, and found every little tin heart a certain night librarian left behind. Now he would like to walk the Long Road with you. Bring a shovel. Joe will count the steps.
